body.proof_tex:
Put \(m_0=|I_0|\).  The deterministic fold-size condition in
\(\mathcal I\) gives \(m_0\ge\lfloor n/K_0\rfloor\ge n/(2K_0)\) for all
sufficiently large \(n\).  For each \((a,k)\),
\(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\) makes
\(N_{ak}^{(0)}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m_0,q_{ak})\), where
\[
 q_{ak}=P_n(X=k,A=a)\ge\epsilon p_k
 \ge\frac{\epsilon c_0}{d_n}.
\tag{1}
\]
The first inequality is \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\), and the second is
\(ass:balanced\text{-}cell\text{-}masses\).  Hence its mean
\(\lambda_{ak}=m_0q_{ak}\) obeys
\[
 \lambda_{ak}\ge\frac{\epsilon c_0n}{2K_0d_n}.
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \(ass:local\text{-}dimension\) implies
\[
 \frac{n}{d_n\log(en)}
 =\frac{\sqrt n}{d_n}\frac{\sqrt n}{\log(en)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus (2) is at least \(512\log(en)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

For completeness, if \(Z\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\) has mean
\(\lambda=mq\), exponential Markov inequality with \(t=\log2\), followed by
\(1+x\le e^x\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P\{Z\le\lambda/2\}
 &\le e^{t\lambda/2}E[e^{-tZ}]
 =e^{t\lambda/2}(1-q+qe^{-t})^m\\
 &\le\exp\{\lambda(t/2+e^{-t}-1)\}
 \le e^{-\lambda/8},
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
because \((\log2)/2-1/2<-1/8\).  Equations (2)--(4) therefore yield
\[
 Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\{N_{ak}^{(0)}\le256\log(en)\}
 \le\exp\!\left(-\frac{\epsilon c_0}{16K_0}\frac n{d_n}\right).
\tag{5}
\]
A union bound over the \(2d_n\) arm-cells, and the harmless enlargement
\(2d_n\le2d_nK_0\), prove the displayed bound.  Finally,
\(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) implies
\(\log(2d_nK_0)-cn/d_n\to-\infty\), proving that its right-hand side is
\(o(1)\).
body.justification: This is the probabilistic bridge that makes an exact all-heavy override useful on the balanced local class.
body.gap: The lemma controls selection only; it asserts no tail property for either proposed confidence radius.
body.consumer: The unresolved heavy-light local theorem uses it to transfer center and variance conclusions from the saturated one-step benchmark.
